info.title: Mediflow API
info.description: Generated from the API route schemas by `pnpm gen:api`. Do not edit by hand.

mfaEnabled.description: Whether sign-in asks for an authenticator code.

isPlatformAdmin.description: A platform operator: has no hospital and no patient data, and uses the platform screens. Steers the screens only; every /platform route checks the flag on the server.

activeTenant.description: Null until a user with several hospitals picks one.

policy.description: Null when there is no active tenant.

needsPassword.description: False when this person already has an account: they only accept.

secret.description: Base32, for typing into an authenticator by hand.

recoveryCodes.description: One-time codes. Returned this once and never again.

id.description: An opaque id for the session, only for ending it. Not the cookie and not derived from it.

userAgent.description: The browser as it described itself at sign-in, cleaned and cut, for the person to recognise the device.

current.description: True for the session making this call.

nextCursor.description: Always null: a person has few sessions.

primary.description: Brand colour as six-digit hex. Must read as text on a white background (contrast of at least 4.5:1); the web app falls back to its default colour otherwise.

logoUrl.description: https or same-origin URL of the hospital logo (SVG or WebP, at most 50 kB).

address.description: Postal address, printed on the letterhead. May hold line breaks.

phone.description: Phone number, printed on the letterhead.

registrationNumber.description: The hospital's registration or licence number as a clinical establishment, printed on the letterhead.

gstin.description: The hospital's GST identification number, printed on invoices.

features.description: Module flags. A module that is absent is off.

idleTimeoutMinutes.description: A session with no activity for this long ends. The web app warns shortly before and signs the user out. Absent means the app default.

staffLimit.description: Only in GET /tenant, not in the session.

max.description: The most staff the hospital may have. Null: no limit.

used.description: Active members plus open invitations. At the limit, POST /invites is 409 user_limit_reached.

status.description: A suspended or offboarding hospital keeps its data but its staff cannot use the app. Tenant-scoped routes answer 403 tenant_suspended.

RoleGrant.description: A permission and the scope it is held at (default all).

PermissionCatalog.description: Every permission the API knows, for the role editor.

scopes.description: The scopes the permission can be held at; always starts with all

HospitalProfile.description: What the hospital prints on its letterhead and invoices. A detail that is not set is absent. Holds no patient data.

version.description: Counts the changes. Sent back as expectedVersion.

Invite.description: An invitation that has been emailed. The link is not returned.

StaffMember.description: Someone who works at the hospital, or has been invited to. For a member `id` is the user id; for an invitation it is the invitation id.

delivery.description: Invitations only: whether the email was sent, is still being tried, or could not be sent (its last attempt failed, or it was never sent within the hour). Never the error or the address it went to.

StaffPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

InviteResent.description: The invitation that is being sent again.

PatientSummary.description: A patient as shown in a list: compact, no clinical data.

phone.description: Masked to its last four digits for a caller without patient.contact:read.

legacyId.description: The registration number from the older register (#694).

mergedInto.description: Present when this record was merged into another (#194, #604): the id of the record to use.

PatientPage.description: Cursor envelope used by every list endpoint.

PatientRecord.description: A registered patient with the details captured at registration. Email and address are left out for a caller without patient.contact:read.

phone.description: Masked to its last four digits for a caller without patient.contact:read.

legacyId.description: The registration number from the older register (#694).

mergedInto.description: Present when this record was merged into another (#194): the id of the record to use. A merged record cannot be changed.

version.description: Goes up by one each time the record changes. Send it back as expectedVersion when changing the record.

PatientUpdate.description: The version the change is based on, and the fields to change. Null clears an optional field. The MRN never changes.

expectedVersion.description: The version of the record the change was made from. If the record has changed since, the request is refused with 409 conflict and nothing is changed.

PatientDuplicateMatch.description: A possible duplicate, masked by the server: enough to recognise the person, not to read their details. No id.

moved.description: How many rows each module moved to the survivor, by module.

expectedVersion.description: The version of the surviving record that was read (409 `conflict` if it moved).

expectedSourceVersion.description: The version of the record being merged away that was read.

moves.description: How many rows each module would move to the survivor, by module; none is zero.

Doctor.description: A doctor profile: a staff member of one hospital, in one department. Holds no patient data.

active.description: False once the doctor no longer practises here, or while their membership of the hospital is deactivated: kept on old records, not offered for new ones.

version.description: Counts the changes. Sent back as expectedVersion.

qualifications.description: Recognised degrees as printed after the name, e.g. "MBBS, MD (General Medicine)".

registrationCouncil.description: The council that gave the registration number: the NMC or a state medical council.

consultationMinutes.description: The usual length of one appointment.

DoctorAvailability.description: Regular weekly working hours. A day without a session is a day off.

ServicePrice.description: What a service costs on one price list from one date. A price is never edited: a new one takes over from its own date.

amountMinor.description: In the minor unit of the hospital's currency.

effectiveFrom.description: A calendar date at the hospital.

effectiveTo.description: The last day it applies. Absent while no later price follows.

Service.description: Something the hospital can charge for. Holds no patient data. code.description: The service's identity on bills. Never changes.

taxClass.description: Which tax rate applies, as a class. The rate of each class is the hospital's tax setting, so a change of rate does not touch the services.

modality.description: The equipment an imaging service is performed on, which sorts radiology’s worklist. Only a service of the category imaging has one.

type.description: A medicine, or a consumable such as gloves or a syringe.

genericName.description: The generic name of a medicine, or what a consumable is.

strength.description: As written on the pack: "500 mg".

unit.description: What one unit of stock is: "strip of 10", "100 ml bottle", "piece".

schedule.description: The drug schedule the item falls under, recorded as a class. What each schedule requires (registers, prescriptions kept) is the pharmacy module's to enforce.

controlled.description: Whether it is handled as a controlled drug. Always true for schedule x and narcotic, whatever is sent.

reorderLevel.description: Stock at or below this many units is low. Absent: no level set.

LabTest.description: A test or a panel the laboratory offers: what it is, how it is collected and how its result is read. Holds no patient data.

code.description: The test's identity on orders and reports. Never changes.

kind.description: A single test, or a panel: a named set of tests ordered together (a lipid profile). A panel has components and no result of its own.

resultType.description: How a result is recorded: a number against a reference range, or text (positive, negative, a description). For a panel it means nothing.

unit.description: The unit of a numeric result: g/dL.

container.description: What the sample is collected in.

turnaroundHours.description: How long a result usually takes from collection.

serviceName.description: The name of the linked service, when there is one. The name alone is shown to everyone who may read the test, by decision; nothing else of the service (a price, a tax class) is ever added here.

components.description: The tests of a panel. Empty for a single test.

LabAge.description: An age as it is written: a value with its unit. Never turned into a count of days: a patient reaches it on the calendar day that lies that long after the date of birth, so leap years and the lengths of months are respected. At most 150 years, in any unit.

LabRange.description: What is normal for one sex in one span of age: from `ageFrom`, included (the day the patient reaches it), until `ageUntil`, not included (that day belongs to the next range). No `ageUntil`: no upper age.

sex.description: Whom the row is for. A row for one sex is used before a row for any.

low.description: The lowest normal value. Absent: no lower limit.

high.description: The highest normal value. Absent: no upper limit.

criticalLow.description: At or below this the result is critical. Only with `low`, and below it.

criticalHigh.description: At or above this the result is critical. Only with `high`, and above it.

LabRangeResolved.description: `range` is absent when no row covers that age and sex.

BedCategory.description: A class of bed (general ward, private room, intensive care), which decides what a day in it is charged as. The charge itself is posted by the admissions module from the linked service, at the price in force that day. An admission keeps the category and the service of its bed as they were when the patient was given it, so a change made here applies to stays that start after it.

serviceName.description: The name of the linked service, when there is one. The name alone is shown to everyone who may read wards, by decision; nothing else of the service (a price, a tax class) is ever added here.

bedCount.description: The beds in use that have this category.

version.description: Counts the changes. Sent back as expectedVersion.

code.description: Short and unique in the hospital. Never changes.

floor.description: Where it is: a floor, a block, a wing.

status.description: available: free to take a patient. occupied: a patient is admitted to it (set by admissions). cleaning: being made ready after a discharge (set by housekeeping). blocked: taken out of use here, with a reason.

blockedNote.description: A few words more about why. About the bed, never about a patient.

BedReleaseReason.description: Why a patient left a bed.

BoardBedStatus.description: available -> occupied (a patient is given the bed) -> cleaning (they leave) -> available (it is ready). blocked is set from the wards API.

bedId.description: An available bed to give the patient now. Left out, the patient is admitted without a bed and given one with assignBed.

sourceEncounterId.description: The visit (OPD, daycare or emergency encounter) of this patient the admission came from. A reference only; 422 `unknown_encounter` when it is not one of theirs.

adviceNote.description: The doctor advice to admit: why, and what to do first. Plain text.

depositMinor.description: The deposit asked for at admission, in minor units. A record only: it is taken through billing.

consents.description: The consents given. Kept as they were at admission.

dayPriceMinor.description: The bed-day price in minor units on the standard list on the day the patient was given the bed, absent when the service has none then.

moveNote.description: Plain text, with the move reason.

stays.description: Every bed the patient was in, oldest first: the bed history.

blockedReason.description: Why a blocked bed is out of use, from a list.

version.description: The bed’s, for setBedHousekeeping.

body.description: The text of a template: the rich text document of the app (paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes and marks), never HTML. Reduced to that allowlist on the way in. Placeholders are plain text in double braces, `{{patient.name}}`. A placeholder is recognised only inside one run of text, for the check and for filling alike: one that is split by formatting (half of it bold) is neither checked nor ever filled, by any part of the system. Names are trimmed and case-sensitive. A value is filled in as text and is never read for placeholders again.

reason.description: Why the version is removed, from a list: free text here could repeat what is being removed.

type.description: How the text becomes the value: `boolean` is yes or no (true, false, y, n, 1, 0); `enum` one of `values`, whatever its capitals; `date` YYYY-MM-DD; `amount` the hospital currency with a point before the minor units, grouped by commas or not.

ImportBatch.description: Records of one kind loaded from a file. It holds counts and codes, never a value of a row.

status.description: staging: rows are being sent. checking: the dry run is running. checked: it has run, and the batch can be written when problemCount is 0. queued, running: being written. committed: every row was written. failed: nothing was written. cancelled: given up, or left unfinished for a week.

doneCount.description: Rows checked while checking, rows written while running.

failure.description: Why nothing was written, as a code: rows_refused (see the problems), permission_withdrawn, write_failed, expired.

ImportRowsUpload.description: Rows of the file, as many requests as it takes. A line sent twice is kept as it was first sent.

fields.description: The fields of the kind the columns of the file were mapped to, in the order of `values`. Each at most once.

values.description: The text of each field of `fields`. An empty text is no value.

ImportProblem.description: Never the value that was refused.

code.description: What is wrong. Of one field: required, not_a_whole_number, not_yes_or_no, not_allowed, not_a_date, not_an_amount, too_many_decimals, invalid, not_found, out_of_range, too_few_digits, not_an_email. QueuePriority.description: Why a token goes ahead of the others.

QueueCancelReason.description: Why a token was taken off the queue.

doctorId.description: A practising doctor of the department (422 `doctor_not_in_department` otherwise).

number.description: The department’s number for the day.

day.description: The calendar day at the hospital.

doctorId.description: Absent while any doctor of the department may call it.

next.description: The numbers next to be called, in call order.

queueTokenId.description: The token the reading was taken for. A correction carries the one of the reading it corrects.

encounterId.description: Set once, from empty to the encounter, by the triage module itself when it hears encounter.opened for the reading’s queue token (idempotently); nothing else of a reading ever changes. temperature.description: Degrees Celsius, at most one decimal.

chiefComplaint.description: Plain text of one or more lines: what brings the patient today, in their words.

correctsId.description: The reading of the same patient this one corrects. The original is kept.

put.description: Saves a new version of a template: the name, the text, or both. Requires template:manage and template:read. post.description: Books an appointment for a patient with a doctor, starting at one of the doctor’s free slots (see `/appointments/free-slots`); the server sets its end from the slot length. Needs `appointment:create`. The Idempotency-Key header is required: a repeat with the same key books nothing and answers with the appointment as it is now. Two bookings can never hold the same doctor at the same time: a database exclusion constraint on the doctor’s scheduled appointments decides between simultaneous requests, and the loser is refused with 409 `slot_taken`. A patient cannot be booked at a time that overlaps one of their own scheduled appointments, with any doctor: 409 `patient_overlap`. A start that is not a slot of the doctor’s working hours, is already past or is more than 90 days ahead is refused with 422 `outside_hours`. An unknown patient or an unknown or inactive doctor gives 422 `unknown_patient` or `unknown_doctor`, the same whether the id belongs to another hospital or to none. `extensions` holds the values of the fields other features add to the booking form (the `appointment.form.fields` slot), keyed by feature id; a part for a feature that registered no schema is refused (422 `unknown_extension`), and no feature registers one yet. The reason is stored as plain text. The answer names the patient (name and MRN) to anyone who may book. Writes `appointment.created` to the outbox and the audit log in the same transaction.

A patient with a token still waiting, called or skipped in that department today is refused (409 `already_queued`, decided by a unique index). An unknown or archived department is 422 `unknown_department`. Requires queue:create and patient:read: a role that may not read patients learns nothing about one here, as an unknown patient and a patient it may not read are both 422 `unknown_patient`. The Idempotency-Key header is required: a repeat issues nothing and answers with the token as it is now. Audited, emits `queue.token_issued` through the outbox, and is announced on `/queue/events`.

An appointment gives one token, ever: checking it in again, from any desk, answers 200 with the token it was given, as it is now (a token outside the caller’s scope of queue:create is refused instead: 409 `already_queued` while it is open, `already_checked_in` once served). An appointment that does not exist, of another hospital or outside the scope the caller holds appointment:read with is 422 `unknown_appointment`; a patient the caller may not read is 422 `unknown_patient`, as for issuing; a doctor who no longer practises here is 422 `unknown_doctor`; a department archived, or outside the caller’s scope of queue:create, is 422 `unknown_department`. A patient with a token still open in that department today is 409 `already_queued`. Requires queue:create, appointment:read and patient:read, and both the queue and the appointments feature flags (403 `feature_disabled`). The Idempotency-Key header is required: a repeat issues nothing and answers with the token as it is now. Audited, emits `queue.token_issued` with the appointment through the outbox, and is announced on `/queue/events`.

get.description: Server-sent events for the queues of the session’s hospital, and of no other. Each `queue` event says only which department’s queue changed (`data: {"departmentId":"..."}`), never who: the screen then reads the queue again through listQueueTokens, which is audited. Under a `queue:read` scope of `department` or `own`, only the caller’s department’s events are sent. The stream opens with a `retry:` line and holds no database connection while open; a comment line is sent every 20 seconds to keep the connection open, and a client takes 45 seconds without anything as a lost connection. The server ends the stream when the session ends, is revoked, goes idle or switches hospital, and when the session loses queue:read or the hospital the queue switch or is suspended, checking all of these again at each keep-alive and before sending events (a check made in the last two seconds is reused for a burst). It also ends the stream when it may have missed changes, so the screen opens it again and reads the queue. 503 `live_unavailable` when live updates cannot be followed now: the screen reads the queue on a timer instead. Requires queue:read and the queue feature flag.
